title: ProtGPS reveals sequence signals that direct proteins to subcellular compartments
summary: ProtGPS, a protein language model and generative sequence-design system, helped identify amino-acid sequence features that guide proteins to subcellular compartments. The paper applies the model to predict disease-mutation-associated localization shifts and reports cellular testing of 20 examples.
ai_technology: ProtGPS protein language model and generative design algorithm
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Whitehead Institute

evidence.tested: The paper applies the model to predict disease-mutation-associated localization shifts and reports cellular testing of 20 examples.
evidence.unknown: The 20 tested mutations are a sample of a much larger computational screen; the predictions do not establish causal disease mechanisms in patients.
evidence.ai_role: ProtGPS predicted compartment localization and mutation-associated shifts, and its generative component designed sequences for target localization. Researchers experimentally tested 20 mutation predictions in cells and reported confirmation.
